answer: LINE (Large-scale Information Network Embedding) improves node classification on citation networks by learning embeddings that preserve local neighborhood structure rather than relying on global graph properties. In practice, it models first-order proximity (directly connected nodes should have similar embeddings) and second-order proximity (nodes with similar neighbors should be close in embedding space). By focusing on these local relationships, LINE captures the most informative citation patterns around each paper, which produces embeddings that are useful as features for downstream node classification and often yields better accuracy than methods that emphasize only global structure or random-walk context.
